question.problem:
Which of the following gives the area bounded between the curve defined parametrically as

$$
x={e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,y=t{e}^{t}
$$

and the $x$-axis for $t\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},0]?$
question.worked_solution:
The unsigned area bounded by the parametric curve 

$$
x=x(t),\,y=y(t),\,{t}_{1}\le t\le {t}_{2}
$$

and the $x$-axis is given by the absolute value of the integral

$$
{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t.
$$

First, we compute

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t) \\  & =-{e}^{-t}\operatorname{sin}⁡t+{e}^{-t}\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\  & ={e}^{-t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t).\end{aligned}
$$

So, we obtain the integral expression

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{{t}_{1}}^{{t}_{2}}y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,\text{d}t & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}t{e}^{t}\cdot {e}^{-t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t \\  & ={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}t(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t.\end{aligned}
$$

Notice that this integral will give us a negative number since $y\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\le 0$ for all $t\in [-\frac{\pi }{2},0].$

Therefore, the area is given by

$$
A=-{\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}t(\operatorname{cos}⁡t-\operatorname{sin}⁡t)\,\text{d}t={\int }_{-\pi /2}^{0}t(\operatorname{sin}⁡t-\operatorname{cos}⁡t)\,\text{d}t.
$$
